note: Adjudicated variants: four of punctuation, two of orthography (the house i/j rule) and one of capital-accent — seven entries, ten readings across three witnesses. Substantive text agrees across all three with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals, and handmissal-eo attests the practice — parallel to the ruling at ordinarium.praefatio-communis w031.

Comma after ut, with witnesses do and mr: the comma sets off the whole quotquot clause, which is embedded inside the purpose clause ut ... repleámur and separates it from the main verb far ahead.
No comma after quotquot, with witnesses do and mr: quotquot is the subject of sumpsérimus and belongs with what follows it.
No comma between the genitive Fílii tui and the nouns it depends on, with witnesses do and mr.
No comma before the apposition Dóminum nostrum, with witnesses handmissal-eo and mr, and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018.
